title: API and GraphQL Security Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: GraphQL introspection enabled
rules.description: A GraphQL schema or server is constructed with introspection=True (Graphene, Strawberry, Ariadne, graphql-core). Introspection publishes the entire schema - every type, field, argument and deprecation - to any unauthenticated caller, which maps the private API surface for an attacker.
rules.remediation_example: schema = graphene.Schema(query=Query)  # keep introspection off in production; expose it only in development

rules.name: Mass assignment from unvalidated request data
rules.description: A model or ORM entity is constructed by unpacking a whole request payload, as in Model(**request.json()) or Model(**await request.json()). Every key the client sends is bound to an attribute, so a caller can set fields the endpoint never intended to expose - role, is_admin, owner_id, balance - which is mass assignment privilege escalation.
rules.remediation_example: data = ModelSchema(**await request.json()); User(**data.model_dump(include=FIELDS))  # bind an explicit allow-list of fields
